spec_match.rationale: Probes the four real prerequisites in the order the spec imposes them — secure context, the [IsolatedContext, SecureContext, RuntimeEnabled=SubApps] window.subApps binding, the sub-apps permission policy (queried only when the token is recognised), and a live subApps.list() call — and correctly explains that binding absence on a plain https origin is by design.

interactive.rationale: A probe button fills a live four-row PASS/FAIL table with the exact measured expression for each gate and a verdict naming the single blocking prerequisite.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the real four-part probe showing exactly which prerequisite blocks the API; the page delivers precisely that, including the honest all-fail state here.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles missing featurePolicy introspection, unrecognised policy tokens (avoiding spurious console warnings), binding-present-but-list-missing, and list() rejection with the exact exception — each with distinct honest messaging.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/6260680824061952, the WICG spec, and the official sample demo with setup README.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the binding, the three methods, secure context, and negative branches; its 1 pass / 6 fail here is the expected absent IWA-only binding in a plain-origin Chromium 141, exactly what this page teaches.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): desktop screenshot shows the pre-probe state with honest placeholder rows; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; the probe button could not be clicked non-interactively, so the populated PASS/FAIL table was verified from code reading only.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts both the available and unavailable gate outcomes with the individual gate booleans.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours, fixed table layout, and amber used only as a border, but the PASS status text renders --accent-emerald bold mono on --bg-paper (~4.1:1), just under WCAG AA 4.5:1 — and at least the secure-context row shows it on any https origin after probing.

accessibility.rationale: Semantic table with caption and scoped headers, role=status aria-live verdict, focusable pre (tabindex=0), and PASS/FAIL conveyed as text not colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (fixed-layout table with overflow-wrap:anywhere); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Darken the PASS emerald to clear AA contrast
openQuestions.detail: td.gate.pass renders --accent-emerald #0a8f5c bold on --bg-paper white at 16px, ~4.1:1 versus the 4.5:1 AA bar, and the secure-context row shows PASS for every https visitor who probes. A darker emerald token fixes it (and the same pattern corpus-wide).

openQuestions.title: Run the probe inside a real Isolated Web App and record the all-gates-pass state
openQuestions.detail: The four-PASS verdict, the live list() resolution, and the recognised sub-apps policy token are only reachable inside a signed IWA on ChromeOS with the three flags — unavailable to this headless session. Follow the page's own setup steps (or the linked subapps-demo README) once and record the passing table as evidence, which also exercises the currently-blocked positive branches of the conformance suite.

summary: An exemplary diagnose-don't-blame capability page: each Sub Apps prerequisite is measured with the real expression and the verdict names the specific blocker, with the plain-origin absence correctly framed as by-design. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): clean pre-probe render and console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either device class. Open items: the marginal PASS emerald contrast and capturing an in-IWA all-pass run.
